headline: The shop is loved. The porch just needs one honest pass.
summary: People can find you. The phone is real. Photos of the work are out there. What is costing you is the small stuff that drifted: hours that do not match from one listing to the next, and a site that works but still feels like a leftover template.

signals.note: You show up. Yelp, maps, and the site all point at a real El Cajon grooming shop, not a ghost.
signals.next: Keep the category and service area tight so "cat groomer near me" still lands on you.

signals.note: The number (619) 449-3388 is the same on the site and the listings. That is rarer than it should be.
signals.next: Call it once a week from a phone that is not yours. Confirm a person still picks up during the hours you advertise.

signals.note: The site says Monday through Saturday, 8:30 to 5. Older posts around town say 8 till done, or 8:30 till 3, and walk-in nail trims at two different windows. A neighbor checking tonight cannot tell which is true.
signals.next: Pick the hours you actually keep. Put that one version on Google, the site, and the door. Then leave it alone until it changes.

signals.note: There are plenty of pictures of real dogs and cats, not stock fluff. The work shows.
signals.next: Add three new photos this month from the actual shop floor so the listing does not freeze in last year.

signals.note: The site loads and tells people who you are. It still has leftover template chrome and reads a little like a brochure that never got a second pass.
signals.next: Keep the family story. Cut the clutter. Make the phone and hours the first thing a thumb can hit.

signals.note: Name and phone line up. Address looks right. Hours do not. That is enough to send someone to a closed door.
signals.next: Match hours everywhere first. That single fix does more than a redesign.
